acceptanceCriteria: Decide and record in docs/specs/cem-stable-v1.md whether an argument-stage refusal (stage arguments, code invalid-arguments, including a bad --trusted-keys file) is REJECT with accept:false or UNSUPPORTED with accept:null, and make the native CLI (internal/cem/cli/stable.go Refuse arguments/invalid-arguments) and both portable commands (interop/cem01-go/stable_repository.go and cem.go failStable with operational invalid-arguments) emit the same outcome and accept value.

A test in internal/cem/verify or cmd/corvint and one in interop/cem01-go run the same bad argument set (missing --map, relative --repository, trusted-keys file with an empty keys array) and assert identical outcome, stage, code and accept.
If the divergence is intentional, record the reason in cem-stable-v1.md next to the CEM-V1-084 parity sentence and close this ticket with that evidence instead.
body: Observed 2026-10-12 by the independent Codex review of the V1-1264 branch (CEM-V1-084 receipt authentication). For the same argument-stage refusal the native stable CLI returns outcome REJECT with accept:false (internal/cem/cli/stable.go, r.Refuse("arguments","invalid-arguments",false)), while both portable commands return outcome UNSUPPORTED with accept:null (interop/cem01-go/stable_repository.go executeStableCanonicalCLI and cem.go, failStable(&r,"arguments",operational("invalid-arguments"),false)). The divergence predates V1-1264: the existing missing or relative --map and --repository refusals use the same calls on origin/main 84c331fca. V1-1264 mirrored each consumer's existing convention for a bad --trusted-keys file rather than changing the argument stage. Reproduce: run corvint cem verify-stable and the portable verify-stable and canonical commands with --trusted-keys pointing at an absolute file holding {"profile":"corvint-trusted-keys/1","keys":[]} and compare the JSON outcome and accept members. Expected under the CEM-V1-084 parity sentence: the same result. Actual: REJECT/false versus UNSUPPORTED/null. Suspected contract gap, not a confirmed verifier defect: the parity requirement may only intend the stages after arguments.
title: cem stable verifiers: argument-stage refusal outcome differs between native (REJECT) and portable (UNSUPPORTED)
